component.name: sparq
component.description: sparq — SOTA Rust RDF + SPARQL engine. This is the checked-in VEX (Vulnerability Exploitability eXchange) source of truth; the release workflow stamps the released version into a per-release copy attached to the GitHub Release alongside the CycloneDX SBOM.

_comment: [OPUS-4.8] sq-toze.3 (GX-2): VEX justifying the advisories that cargo-deny is configured
to ignore in deny.toml. KEEP THIS IN SYNC WITH deny.toml [advisories].ignore — each entry
here corresponds 1:1 to an ignore there, with the same justification.
[OPUS-5] sq-5ah3p: RUSTSEC-2025-0134 (`rustls-pemfile`) is REMOVED AGAIN, and for the second
time by deletion rather than tolerance. It first left under sq-g2xs when the federation HTTP
client moved ureq 2 -> ureq 3 (rustls-native-certs 0.8 dropped the archived crate); it returned
with the solid-server-rs import, which parsed its mTLS PEM material through rustls-pemfile 2.
sparq-lws-core's `tls.rs` and sparq-server's `main.rs` now call rustls-pki-types' `PemObject`
directly through rustls' own `pki_types` re-export, so no workspace crate declares the archived
shim and it is absent from Cargo.lock. The deny.toml ignore, the cargo-vet exemption and this
VEX statement were dropped together to keep the 1:1 invariant, and the gate now re-flags any
regression that reintroduces the crate.
When a future advisory needs a justified ignore, add the
deny.toml ignore AND the matching VEX statement here together, with the HONEST analysis.state
(`not_affected` ONLY when genuinely so; `exploitable` when the vulnerable code is present and
reachable but cannot be fixed at sparq's level yet).
[OPUS-4.8] sq-iywur: RUSTSEC-2026-0194 (quick-xml < 0.41 quadratic duplicate-attribute DoS) and
RUSTSEC-2026-0195 (quick-xml < 0.41 unbounded NsReader namespace-declaration allocation, a
memory-exhaustion DoS) are BOTH recorded below as `exploitable` (NOT not_affected): sparq's own
RDF/XML parse paths are on the patched 0.41, but the transitive quick-xml 0.37.5 pinned by the
oxigraph 0.5.x stack IS reachable when oxigraph parses untrusted RDF/XML and has no fixed
upstream release yet. Both are fixed by the same upgrade (>= 0.41.0).
[GPT-5.6] sq-cx4w2: RUSTSEC-2024-0436 records that paste is unmaintained, not a
vulnerability. parquet 59 reintroduces it for sparq-arrow's default-OFF parquet feature;
remove the deny ignore and matching VEX statement together when parquet drops paste.

vulnerabilities.description: paste is archived and no longer maintained. This is an informational maintenance-status advisory: it reports no vulnerability, CVE, or known exploit.
vulnerabilities.detail: [GPT-5.6] parquet 59 pulls paste 1.0.15 transitively for sparq-arrow's separate default-OFF parquet feature. parquet currently publishes no paste-free release, so sparq cannot remove this transitive crate without dropping the requested Parquet capability.

analysis.detail: The advisory describes project maintenance status rather than vulnerable behavior, so there is no exploit path to reach. The proc macro is present only while compiling the opt-in parquet dependency closure and is absent from default sparq-arrow, lean core, and WebAssembly builds. Follow-up bead sq-cx4w2 tracks parquet upstream; remove this statement and the matching deny.toml ignore together once parquet drops paste.

vulnerabilities.description: bincode 1.3.3 is permanently unmaintained. This is an informational maintenance-status advisory with no reported vulnerability, CVE, or known exploit.
vulnerabilities.detail: [SONNET-4.6] hdt 0.7.3 pulls bincode 1.3.3 transitively through qwt 0.4.0. No maintained bincode release is available on that dependency path.

analysis.detail: The advisory concerns maintenance status rather than vulnerable behavior. sparq does not deserialize attacker-controlled bincode data; bincode is an internal qwt serialization dependency below the opt-in HDT surface. Remove this statement and the matching deny.toml ignore together when hdt/qwt replaces bincode.

vulnerabilities.description: quick-xml before 0.41 takes quadratic time checking a start tag for duplicate attribute names, so an attacker who controls the XML input can cause a denial of service (excessive CPU) with a crafted start tag carrying many attributes. Availability impact only — this is NOT a memory-safety issue and has no known code-execution vector.
vulnerabilities.detail: Two copies of quick-xml were present in the tree. sparq's OWN RDF/XML and SPARQL-Results-XML parse paths (sparq-conformance, sparq-engine `service`, sparq-geo) were bumped 0.40 -> the patched 0.41 and are fixed. The copy this VEX statement covers is the TRANSITIVE quick-xml 0.37.5 pinned by the oxigraph 0.5.x stack (oxrdfxml 0.2.3 / sparesults 0.3.3 / spareval 0.2.6). oxigraph has published no release that moves off quick-xml 0.37, so this transitive copy cannot be upgraded without an upstream oxigraph bump. Tracked in bead sq-iywur; upstream announcement https://github.com/tafia/quick-xml/issues/969.

analysis.detail: Honest reachability: the vulnerable duplicate-attribute check in quick-xml 0.37.5 IS reachable when oxigraph parses untrusted RDF/XML (oxrdfxml) or SPARQL-Results-XML (sparesults), so this is deliberately NOT marked not_affected. It cannot be fixed at sparq's level — no oxigraph release off quick-xml 0.37 exists yet and oxigraph does not expose the quick-xml version as a feature knob. Mitigation: sparq's own (non-oxigraph) XML parse paths are already on the patched 0.41; operators exposing oxigraph-backed RDF/XML ingest to untrusted input should bound request/body size at the perimeter. Impact is availability-only (quadratic CPU), not memory-unsafety. Remove this statement AND the matching deny.toml [advisories].ignore entry once oxigraph ships a quick-xml >= 0.41 release. Mirrors the deny.toml [advisories].ignore entry (same reason).

vulnerabilities.description: quick-xml before 0.41, when namespace resolution is used (`NsReader`, or a direct `NamespaceResolver::push`), allocates one namespace-binding entry per namespace declaration on a start tag with no upper bound, so an attacker who controls the XML input can exhaust process memory (OOM) with a crafted start tag carrying a very large number of `xmlns:` declarations. Availability impact only — a memory-exhaustion denial of service, NOT a memory-safety (unsound) issue, and with no known code-execution vector.
vulnerabilities.detail: Same two-copy situation and same fix as RUSTSEC-2026-0194. sparq's OWN RDF/XML and SPARQL-Results-XML parse paths (sparq-conformance, sparq-engine `service`, sparq-geo) were bumped 0.40 -> the patched 0.41 and are fixed (0.41 caps declarations per element via NamespaceResolver::set_max_declarations_per_element). The copy this VEX statement covers is the TRANSITIVE quick-xml 0.37.5 pinned by the oxigraph 0.5.x stack (oxrdfxml 0.2.3 / sparesults 0.3.3 / spareval 0.2.6). oxigraph has published no release that moves off quick-xml 0.37, so this transitive copy cannot be upgraded without an upstream oxigraph bump. Tracked in bead sq-iywur; upstream announcement https://github.com/tafia/quick-xml/issues/970.

analysis.detail: Honest reachability: oxigraph's RDF/XML reader (oxrdfxml) performs namespace resolution via quick-xml's NsReader, so the unbounded namespace-declaration allocation in quick-xml 0.37.5 IS reachable when oxigraph parses untrusted RDF/XML — this is deliberately NOT marked not_affected. It cannot be fixed at sparq's level — no oxigraph release off quick-xml 0.37 exists yet and oxigraph does not expose the quick-xml version as a feature knob, nor the new per-element declaration cap. Mitigation: sparq's own (non-oxigraph) XML parse paths are already on the patched 0.41; operators exposing oxigraph-backed RDF/XML ingest to untrusted input should bound request/body size at the perimeter. Impact is availability-only (memory exhaustion / OOM), not memory-unsafety. Remove this statement AND the matching deny.toml [advisories].ignore entry once oxigraph ships a quick-xml >= 0.41 release. Mirrors the deny.toml [advisories].ignore entry (same reason).
